thread:
Anya: quick thing — found a bad UX when authoring route YAML in Console. I added a header override block and the linter errors out.

Anya: example snippet I pasted into Console:```yaml
route:
  match: /v1/chat/*
  backend: redwood-chat
  headers:
    override:
      x-customer-id: '{{customer.id}}'
      x-tier: premium
``` 

Anya: linter returns: `headers: additionalProperties not allowed` even though Console supports header overrides at runtime. 😕

LintBot: CI lint-check failed on branch feature/routing-lint — schema error: /route/headers: "additionalProperties" violation (rule: routing-schema-v2)

Mike: thanks — this is because our openapi-ish schema treats `headers` as a strict map of exact keys (x-allowed-headers) and doesn't allow nested `override` objects. We tightened it to prevent arbitrary blobs, but Console wants a small structured override block.

Sara: two options:
- widen schema to accept `headers.override` as an object with free-form string values, and add a lint rule to forbid templates except {{}} style, or
- keep schema strict and change Console to emit `overridesHeaders` flattened map so it's validated by current schema.

Jeff: prefer widening the schema. It's backwards compatible if we add an optional `override` property with type object and `additionalProperties: { type: string }`. Then put stricter lint-checks on template usage in our linter rules instead of in base JSON schema.

Design: for Console UX I'd like an inline hint and a quick-fix button that converts the nested `override` block to the flattened form (or vice-versa) so users don't get blocked.

Anya: +1 on quick-fix. For validation flow, can we run a preflight dry-run from the editor before saving? If the lint errors, show explicit quick-fix suggestions.

Mike: we can implement preflight via the /validate-route API that returns both schema errors and lint suggestions. Proposal: add a `suggestedFixes` array to the response with locations and patch snippets.

Sara: will need tests: add unit tests for the linter harness with both YAML and JSON authoring. Example jest test sketch:
```js
it('allows headers.override with string templates', async () => {
  const yaml = `route:\n  match: /x\n  headers:\n    override:\n      x-user: '{{id}}'`;
  const res = await validateRoute(yaml);
  expect(res.errors).toHaveLength(0);
  expect(res.suggestedFixes).toEqual([]);
});
```

Jeff: also add an integration test that runs Console's editor -> /validate-route -> save workflow so we catch UI serialization bugs.

LintBot: created issue #4123: "route schema: allow headers.override as object + lint rule for templates" and linked PR draft: https://git.redwood.local/r/redwood/infra/pulls/765

Mike: I'll update the JSON Schema and add a composed lint rule that forbids functions in header values (no function calls), but allow moustache-style templates. 

Anya: one more: let's add an Editor warning if the header value contains a raw secret-like pattern (e.g., AWS_KEY=) — don't allow accidental secret injection.

Sara: good call. Add a test case for that rule.

Design: I'll mock quick-fix UX in Figma and share a screenshot later.

Jeff: timeline — schema change + linter + unit tests in this sprint? If so, tag me for review on the PR.

Anya: thanks folks. I'll keep the Console-side UX tasks in the same epic. Ping me if you need help with test data for the integration runs. :thumbsup:
